## Each person's records

People add records; each signed-in person sees only their own, with status and
history. The owner sees and updates all records. People request changes by
appending linked change rows, preserving the original record and its history.

Example uses: shop orders, RSVPs and event sign-ups, bookings and appointments, applications (jobs, clubs, hackathons), support requests, homework or assignment submissions, survey answers people can revisit, and a waitlist with “my place in line”.

Use this pattern when someone asks for any of these. Choose resource and table
names that fit the domain (`bookings`, `applications`, and so on), keeping
the `records` preset, a status column and a
linked change table in the same database. Declare its foreign key so a person's
change rows can reference only their own record. This pattern is for hosted
Simple Host and small-box installs.

### Worked example: shop orders

Create an `orders` SQLite resource with `storage_set_resource(site,"orders",body)`
(or owner PUT):

```json
{"kind":"sqlite","preset":"records","site_passcode":"inherit"}
```

Through owner `storage_sql_schema`, create these tables in two calls in that
same database:

```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL,
                     quantity INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT DEFAULT 'placed',
                     created_at TEXT)
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE order_changes (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('change','note','cancel_request')),
  details TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT
)
```

Both tables use the resource's `records` preset (add signed-in, read own, edit and delete owner). The server
adds indexed `visitor_id TEXT`, stamps `created_at` on visitor inserts, and
ignores client-sent identity and timestamps. A declared foreign key checks that
the referenced order exists and belongs to the same customer, in the insert
transaction (404 `invalid_reference` for a missing order and for another customer's order alike).

Customers never rewrite or delete a placed order. They customise it by adding
a change, a note, a cancellation request or a requested new quantity to
`order_changes`; the original order and change history remain. The page shows
“My orders”, each current status and its history, using two reads and matching
`order_changes.order_id` to `orders.id` in the page. There is no `include=` option.

```html
<script>window.SH_CONFIG = {site: 'pantry'};</script>
<script src="https://golden-host.invalid/auth.js"></script>
```

```js
await SH.requireSignIn();
const db = SH.storage.sqlite('orders');
const orders = db.table('orders');
const changes = db.table('order_changes');
const receipt = await orders.add({item: 'Chai spice', quantity: 2});
await changes.add({order_id: receipt.last_insert_id, kind: 'change',
                   details: 'Please change the quantity to 3'});
const mine = await orders.list({order: 'id', desc: 1, limit: 50});
const history = await changes.list({order: 'id', limit: 100});
// Both results contain only this customer's rows. Match history by order_id.
// Follow each next_after cursor with the same order and direction.
```

The owner sees all orders and history through `storage_sql_query`. Each row's
`visitor_id` in connector results is an opaque reference scoped to this site, not an account ID. Pass it directly in `storage_sql_query` or `storage_sql_execute` params for the same site. It lasts until the server restarts; read the row again if needed. Only when the owner asks "who placed order 12?" read
`SELECT visitor_id FROM orders WHERE id = 12` and pass it to
`storage_visitor_emails`, which gives the email they signed in with. Tell the person; never
write the email into a page or into saved data. REST keeps its existing visitor IDs; use those with the owner-only `GET /v1/sites/<site>/storage/visitors?id=<id>` route. The owner's
view applies or acknowledges requests and updates the order's status or stage
with `storage_sql_execute`, for example `UPDATE orders SET status=? WHERE id=?`
with params `["packed",17]`. Keep the history when handling a request. Use the
trusted owner dashboard/connector, or an admin page on the site (`get_page_recipe`
topic `admin`): the owner signed in there with their account email lists every
order (`orders.list({where:{status:'placed'}})`) and sets a status
(`orders.edit(17, {status:'packed'})`). Never put an owner key in a page. The
trade-off of an admin page: while the owner is signed in on their own site, a bug
or a malicious script on its pages could act on that site's data, so write
visitors' text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.

### The owner adds a row for one person (SIM-358)

On a `records` or `personal` table, the owner may add a row on behalf of one
already-signed-in person instead of waiting for them to add it — a coach
assigning a client's program, a tutor replying to a student's message. The
row's `visitor_id` becomes that person's, exactly as if they had added it
themselves, and a second server-owned column, `written_by`, reads `"owner"`
(otherwise `""`, including a plain add with no `for`) so the person's own
reads never mistake it for their own write:

```js
// On the page, signed in as the owner on the site's own address.
await SH.storage.sqlite('orders').table('orders').add(
  {item: 'House blend, 1 lb'}, {for: pickedVisitorId}
);
```

`storage_sql_execute` reaches the same path from a connector, by giving
`table` and `values` instead of `sql` and `params`:

```json
{"site": "<site>", "name": "orders", "for": "client@example.com",
 "table": "orders", "values": {"item": "House blend, 1 lb"}}
```

`for` only ever applies to a table whose read is `own` (`records`, `personal`)
— refused `for_requires_own` on anything wider (`public`, `inbox`, `wall`,
`comments`, `board`, `private`), where the row would otherwise be visible, or
attributed, beyond that one person. `for` takes a `visitor_id` or the email
that person signed in with (matched against their current sign-in email the
same way `storage_visitor_emails`/`SH.me()` do, among people the server
recorded as signed in on this site — never a raw username or OAuth-identity
row alone, and never a guess among more than one match: `visitor_unknown`
(404) if nobody matches, `visitor_email_ambiguous` if more than one does).
There is no email binding before a first sign-in. It never fires
`record.added` to the owner's own webhook subscriptions. `written_by` is
added lazily, under the write lock, the first time a table is used this way
— an existing `records`/`personal` table works without resaving its preset —
and is refused (`written_by_blocked`) rather than risk reshaping a table a
trigger or view depends on; a trigger that got written_by onto the table
some other way, and then rewrites it as a side effect of a `for` insert, is
caught after the fact and the whole add is rolled back
(`written_by_tampered`). The owner's raw SQL console (`storage_sql_execute`
without `for`) refuses a statement naming `written_by`, in `execute` and
`schema` alike, so a new trigger or view cannot name it either — but this
is a name match, not a parser: a positional `INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)`
naming no column is not caught, by design (no SQL parsing was added to try
to catch it). As always, raw SQL can still set `visitor_id` directly too.
Provenance through `written_by` holds for rows added through the table
routes, `auth.js`, and `for`; the raw SQL console remains exactly as
unrestricted on server columns as it already was. Changing a table's
preset later from `records`/`personal` to a wider read exposes an
owner-added row the same as any other row there — expected behaviour of
changing a preset, not specific to this feature. `for`, the pick list, and
`storage_visitor_emails`'s `emails` direction
are Host only (404 on Simple Hack and event storage): named viewers and this
email resolution are not a Simple Hack concept. The owner's pick list of
whom to add for: `SH.storage.people()` on the page, or
`GET /v1/sites/<site>/storage/people` with the owner's key — people who have
saved data here or are named viewers, each confirmed against the server's
own sign-in record, never everyone who has merely signed in and never a raw
table's content taken on trust. `storage_visitor_emails` also takes `emails`
now, resolving each to the reference `for` takes, the same direction REST's
`?email=` does. Worked example: `get_page_recipe` topic `people`.

Create a `photos` file bucket. Choose preset `wall` for photos that visitors may
view (authors can remove their own), or `records` for photos only the sender and
the shop owner see:

```json
{"kind":"files","preset":"wall","site_passcode":"inherit"}
```

```js
await SH.requireSignIn();
// preparedPhoto is a resized WebP Blob, below the single-upload cap.
await SH.storage.files('photos').put(crypto.randomUUID() + '.webp', preparedPhoto);
```

A page may instead call relative REST routes with `credentials:'same-origin'`
and `X-SH-CSRF: 1` for POST/PUT. The server takes identity from the site session.
Preserve the form on a refusal; never widen access to make a save work.

### The same pattern for bookings

Name the SQLite resource `bookings`, keeping the same policies. Through the
owner schema route, create these tables in two calls:

```sql
CREATE TABLE bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, appointment TEXT NOT NULL,
                       status TEXT DEFAULT 'requested', created_at TEXT)
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE booking_changes (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  booking_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES bookings(id),
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('change','note','cancel_request')),
  details TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT
)
```

The server adds indexed `visitor_id TEXT` to both tables as in the orders
example. People add bookings and linked change rows; “My bookings” reads both
tables and matches `booking_changes.booking_id` to `bookings.id`. Each person
sees only their own status and history. The owner reads all bookings and
changes, and updates status (for example, `confirmed`) through owner SQL.



Storage security (2026-10-06, both reviews completed; hosted deployment verified):
Visitor inserts use `INSERT OR ABORT`; visitors cannot supply any primary-key or
rowid value. Use `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` so the server assigns IDs. The inserted
ID comes from `RETURNING`, including for reference checks, never connection-global
insert state. `foreign_keys=ON` is explicit on every SQLite connection. Declare
foreign keys for linked history; undeclared application links are not checked.
A visitor's reference must point at a row they may read under the parent table's
preset (for `own`, a row they added); unreadable and missing parents both return
404 `invalid_reference`. Optional links must be entirely NULL; partly NULL
composite references are refused. Parents without `visitor_id TEXT` fail closed.

Omitting `write_mode` on an existing resource preserves its mode (older fields). Switching a
legacy SQLite database that pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own requires every application table to be empty,
even if earlier rows already carry a `visitor_id`: raw full-mode identities are
not trusted. Clear/migrate those rows deliberately through owner tools first.
Existing own databases keep their stamped rows during policy edits. Unattributed
KV/files remain owner-only under own reads; full-mode visitor overwrites record
the latest writer, while owner overwrites preserve attribution.

Visitor writes use `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_IP` (120,100ms) per site and client IP
and `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_VISITOR` (60,200ms) per site and signed-in visitor.
Reads, including POST `/query`, have no new rate limit; a 150-photo public
gallery loads without consuming write tokens. Owner credentials are exempt.
Reads never take the deploy mutex. Bodies are consumed before locking writes
and quota checks. `SITE_STORAGE_WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` defaults to 2000; writes
during deploy wait briefly, then return 503 `storage_busy` with Retry-After.
Owner operations have `SITE_STORAGE_OWNER_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000); visitor writes
have `SITE_STORAGE_VISITOR_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` (2000), and visitor SQLite queries
have `SITE_STORAGE_VISITOR_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (1000). All SQLite executions,
including owner queries and policy validation, share a process-wide semaphore:
`SITE_STORAGE_SQL_CONCURRENCY=0` selects the CPU count. When full,
`SITE_STORAGE_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS` (250) bounds waiting, then returns 503 with
Retry-After. Writers always take the site lock before the SQLite slot. A visitor's fixed route permits at most 100
columns; the complete JSON query result is bounded by
`SITE_STORAGE_SQL_RESULT_MAX_BYTES`. GET and HEAD are reads.

KV allowance counts UTF-8 key bytes plus normalized JSONB value bytes.
`SITE_STORAGE_FILES_MAX_OBJECTS` defaults to 1000 committed objects per bucket,
including empty/tiny files (507 `bucket_full`). File paths allow at most 16
segments. Own file lists use the existing `(site,resource,writer,path)` index
and LIMIT before opening files; temporary `.upload-*` objects never appear.
New keys and upload paths are normalized to NFC, including macOS decomposed
names. Reads, deletes, listing prefixes and cursors accept exact legacy names.
Own-list cursors follow scanned metadata so missing files cannot end paging early. SQLite uniqueness failures use a generic 409 `row_conflict`; schema
names are not reflected to visitors. 507 `sqlite_full` describes engine
allocation failures separately from the quota precheck's `site_full`.

UNIQUE columns, KV keys and file paths are global within their table/resource.
A failed create can reveal a collision; use opaque random identifiers or a
visitor-specific namespace, never sensitive emails as unique keys. The server
does not silently change owner-defined global uniqueness. `auth.js` retains raw
query/execute for legacy full-mode compatibility; they are owner-only on add/own
resources, and new visitor pages use `table().add/list`. `site_passcode:off` is
an explicit owner choice: public resources stay accessible without unlocking.

The shared clientIP helper still trusts the last X-Forwarded-For entry (N4).
Deploy behind a local proxy that appends the real client address and prevents
direct access to the app port; bare unproxied installs can spoof IP buckets.
entries.new: # Site storage resources: KV, SQLite and files Use owner-defined resources for new sites: KV for named JSON values, SQLite for related records and queries, files for photos and downloads. Resource names are unique across kinds and kinds cannot change. Create resources and SQLite tables before publishing pages that use them. Pages use same-origin REST and site-scoped visitor sign-in; they never contain an owner key. ## Row rules for SQLite and key-value data Follow the description of `storage_set_resource` that this server gives. If it does not accept `rules`, the server is older and its description says what to send. A KV namespace still in Postgres cannot accept rules. File buckets keep presets; their choices are listed separately below. Rules have `version: 1` and `policies`. A policy has a `command`, optional `name`, optional `restrictive: true` (default false), and these clauses: | Command | `using` | `check` | |---|---|---| | `read` | required: stored row | refused | | `add` | refused | required: stored inserted row | | `edit` | required: stored row | optional; inherits using | | `delete` | required: stored row | refused | | `all` | required for read/edit/delete | optional; inherits using for add/edit | Permissive policies OR together; restrictive policies AND together, then narrow that grant. Without an applicable permissive policy, the operation is denied. An empty list denies every page caller, including owner-on-site; owner tools still work. Expressions use columns (`visitor_id` or `row.visitor_id`), trusted bindings, `true`, `false`, `&&`, `||`, `!`, parentheses, `==`, `!=`, `in`, `contains`, `is null`, `is not null`, and ASCII `lower()`. No SQL or ordering operators. Strings use single/double quotes with JSON escapes; lists contain 1–64 strings or numbers of one type. Text compares as case-sensitive bytes. NULL or wrong storage types make both a comparison and its rewritten negation false; test NULL explicitly. Columns match schema names case-insensitively; use `row.in` for a reserved word. Limits and the complete grammar are in [the language reference](https://github.com/vineetu/simple-host/blob/main/docs/designs/storage-rules.md). Platform facts: nullable `auth.id`, boolean `auth.signed_in`, `auth.role` (`anon`, `visitor`, `owner`), boolean `auth.ai`, and `auth.teams` (empty text list without a product). `auth.checked` is declared only with the spam check configured and may appear only in an add check. Every OR alternative of a permissive edit/delete/all using must positively require `auth.signed_in`, `visitor_id == auth.id`, or `auth.role == "owner"` as an AND term. A guard only in check is insufficient. Suspended visitors are refused for identity-dependent permissive policies; a public read of `true` still reads what anyone reads. For bookings, orders, applications or assignments: signed-in people add, each reads their own, and the owner reads and changes all. Recipe topics `booking`, `records` and `people` give complete pages; topic names are unchanged. ```json {"kind":"sqlite","rules":{"version":1,"policies":[ {"command":"read","using":"visitor_id == auth.id || auth.role == \"owner\""}, {"command":"add","check":"auth.signed_in"}, {"command":"edit","using":"auth.role == \"owner\""}, {"command":"delete","using":"auth.role == \"owner\""} ]}} ``` For owner-maintained public data, use read `using: "true"` and an all policy `using: "auth.role == \"owner\""`. For an owner-only inbox, keep that owner policy and use add `check: "true"`. For personal editable notes use all `using: "visitor_id == auth.id || auth.role == \"owner\""`, `check: "auth.signed_in"`. A signed-in condition alone shares rows among people; it does not give per-person privacy. SQLite `tables: {"orders": {"rules": {...}}}` replaces the default set for that table. Omit `tables` to keep existing sets; `{}` removes them. When replacing old table access choices, send each table's rules or `{}`. Do not mix rules and preset fields in a single save. Saving only passcode inheritance keeps rules. Rules responses have `rules_status`, `rules_errors` and table sets. Repair `invalid_rules` using `rule_error` clause and position; `rules_invalid` means a stored set no longer compiles. Do not widen access to fix a refusal. For moderated posts use a checked add plus a restrictive read policy: `{"command":"read","restrictive":true,"using":"auth.role == \"owner\" || approved_at is not null"}`. A table holds posts only when its effective set references TEXT `approved_at`. Visitor adds store NULL; owner-on-site and owner tools stamp the time, unless owner tools supply a value. Only those owner paths may edit the stamp. An unreferenced leftover column is ordinary data. Checked posts get size/link limits; without a configured spam check use signed-in posting and its recipe. Pages use `SH.storage.sqlite(db).table(t).list/get/add/edit/delete`. `SH.storage.toObjects(result)` yields objects with `mine`; other visitors' authors are blanked. The server stamps identity/timestamps and assigns IDs. Edit and delete require read visibility of the stored row. Check failures roll back; hidden and missing rows return the same 404. References must point at rows readable under the parent table's rules. Raw query/execute are owner tools. KV offers `.get`, `.set`, `.keys`, `.delete`; a set adds or edits according to existence and keeps the original author on edit. Rules may name `key`, `value` (normalized JSON text), `visitor_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. A UNIQUE conflict can reveal a hidden row; a KV add attempt can reveal a key's existence via `key_exists`. Use opaque random names, never sensitive keys. The owner signed in on the site's own address uses the same visitor routes and rules with `auth.role == "owner"`; `SH.me()` returns `site_owner: true`. This covers saved data only. Write visitor text with `textContent`. Framed pages and old-version previews never gain these rights. Site passcodes and named viewers, CSRF, quotas and product gates still apply whatever rules say. `site_passcode` is `inherit` by default; `off` is an explicit owner choice. | Task | Connector | REST suffix after `/v1/sites/{site}/storage` | |---|---|---| | List resources and policies | `storage_list_resources(site)` | `GET /resources` (owner) | | Check storage allowance | `storage_get_usage(site)` | `GET /usage` (owner); returns `used_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `remaining_bytes` and `breakdown` by KV, SQLite and files | | Create or change a resource | `storage_set_resource(site,name,body)` | `PUT /resources/{name}` (owner) | | Permanently delete a resource | `storage_delete_resource(site,name)` | `DELETE /resources/{name}` (owner) | | List KV entries | `storage_list_kv_keys(site,name,prefix?,after?,limit?)` | `GET /kv/{name}/keys?prefix=&after=&limit=` | | Read, set, remove a KV value | `storage_get_kv`, `storage_put_kv`, `storage_delete_kv` with `site,name,key` (`value` on put) | `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE /kv/{name}/keys/{key}`; PUT body `{ "value": }` | | Read-only SQL query | `storage_sql_query(site,name,sql,params?)` | `POST /sqlite/{name}/query` with `{sql,params}` | | Change SQL rows | `storage_sql_execute(site,name,sql,params?)` | `POST /sqlite/{name}/execute` with `{sql,params}` | | Change SQL schema | `storage_sql_schema(site,name,sql,params?)` | `POST /sqlite/{name}/schema` (owner) | | List file objects | `storage_list_file_objects(site,name,prefix?,after?,limit?)` | `GET /files/{name}/objects?prefix=&after=&limit=` | | Upload or remove a file | `storage_put_file(site,name,path,content_base64,content_type)`, `storage_delete_file(site,name,path)` | `PUT` raw bytes with `Content-Type`, `DELETE /files/{name}/objects/{path...}` | | Download a file | `storage_file_download_link(site,name,path)` for the owner | Browser or direct REST: `GET /files/{name}/objects/{path...}`; connector mints a scoped ten-minute link rather than returning base64 bytes | The connector's inline file upload is capped at 1 MiB decoded; use direct REST for larger files. File storage is durable across website publishes and rollbacks; it is separate from the versioned website files. Stored raster images may render inline only after the server validates their bytes; other types download as attachments. Do not use a file object as a way to serve arbitrary HTML or JS under the site's origin. KV/SQLite share **10,000,000 bytes per website**; Host files get a separate **10 MB** allowance. Hack retains the pooled allowance across all three kinds. Check `storage_get_usage` or owner-only `GET /usage` before large writes. The response separates `kv_bytes`, `sqlite_bytes` (the main database after checkpoint) and `files_bytes`; SQLite's transient WAL is excluded. This allowance does not include deployed website files or legacy saved data, which retain their own limits. A rejected growth write returns `site_full` without changing the stored value or object. For a page that lets people upload phone photos, resize and compress the image in the browser before sending its bytes to the files API. Decode with `createImageBitmap`, draw to a canvas at a smaller width and height while preserving aspect ratio, and encode as WebP or JPEG with a suitable quality. Choose a target well below the site's remaining allowance so more than one image can fit. Show a preview and the compressed byte size; if it is still too large, explain that the visitor must choose a smaller image or reduce quality. Leave PDFs and other binary files untouched unless the application explicitly defines a conversion. The raw-file API stores the bytes it receives. For example, a browser page can prepare a selected photo before calling `SH.storage.files('photos').put(path, preparedPhoto)`. Its 350,000-byte target fits several photos in the separate 10 MB file allowance; choose a lower target if `/usage` shows less space remains. Show the returned file in an image preview and display its `size` before uploading. If preparation throws, show its message beside the file input and do not upload the original photo. ```js async function preparePhoto(file, maxBytes = 350000) { if (!(file instanceof Blob) || !file.type.startsWith('image/')) throw new TypeError('Choose a photo'); if (!('createImageBitmap' in window)) throw new Error('This browser cannot resize photos'); const image = await createImageBitmap(file); try { const maxEdge = Math.max(image.width, image.height); if (!maxEdge) throw new Error('Photo has no dimensions'); const firstScale = Math.min(1, 1600 / maxEdge); for (let shrink = 1; shrink >= 0.2; shrink *= 0.8) { const canvas = document.createElement('canvas'); canvas.width = Math.max(1, Math.round(image.width * firstScale * shrink)); canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.round(image.height * firstScale * shrink)); const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d'); if (!ctx) throw new Error('This browser cannot draw photos'); ctx.drawImage(image, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height); for (const quality of [0.82, 0.68, 0.54]) { const blob = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => canvas.toBlob( b => b ? resolve(b) : reject(new Error('Photo encoding failed')), 'image/webp', quality)); if (blob.type !== 'image/webp') throw new Error('This browser cannot encode WebP photos'); if (blob.size <= maxBytes) { const name = (file.name || 'photo').replace(/\.[^.]+$/, '') + '.webp'; return new File([blob], name, {type: 'image/webp'}); } } } throw new Error('Photo is still too large; choose a smaller image'); } finally { image.close(); } } ``` SQLite accepts one statement per call with bound positional `?` parameters. A refused statement returns a `sql_*` code and says what to change (the owner's messages list the real tables or columns); fix that rather than resending it. `/query` is read-only; `/execute` changes rows; `/schema` is owner-only for schema changes. The server's SQLite authorizer enforces operation and resource boundaries, including nested statements. The query answer has `columns` and `rows` (BLOB cells are `{ "base64": "..." }`); execute returns `changes` and `last_insert_id`. Design tables and indexes for the actual site; never concatenate visitor text into SQL. For browser calls, use relative `/v1/sites/{site}/storage/...` URLs on the site's own address. Use `SH.requireSignIn()` when the chosen policy requires sign-in and the existing hosted auth helper for the site's session. Visitor writes send the same-site `Origin` and `X-SH-CSRF: 1`; owner tool calls use their existing credential. Treat `sign_in_required` (401), `forbidden` or `site_locked` (403), `resource_not_found` (404), validation errors (400), and `site_full` (507) as server decisions. Do not retry a write with a broader policy merely to make it succeed. Older state, collections and declared-data APIs are deprecated for new work. Maintain existing sites deliberately; their history and withdrawal behavior do not transfer automatically. For privacy use the author condition above. Visitors use fixed table routes with `where` equality filters (at most three), order, direction, limit and an opaque `after` cursor. Keep order and direction when following `next_after`. Defaults are rowid ascending and 100 rows (max 500). Use ordinary rowid tables and `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. Optional composite foreign keys must be entirely NULL. Triggers and cascades that write other rows are refused. Owner SQL remains parameterized and bounded. Simple Host KV and SQLite share **10,000,000 bytes per website** (`SITE_STORAGE_MAX_BYTES`). Files have a separate **10,000,000 bytes per website** (`SITE_STORAGE_FILES_MAX_BYTES`, decimal 10 MB). The usage response keeps `used_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `remaining_bytes` for KV/SQLite and adds `files_used_bytes`, `files_limit_bytes`, `files_remaining_bytes`, retaining the three-kind `breakdown`. The existing single-upload cap remains 1,000,000 bytes (`SITE_STORAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES`); visitor upload pages shrink photos in the browser. SQLite WAL, deployed website files and legacy saved data retain their separate accounting. Simple Hack keeps its existing 1,000,000-byte pool across all three kinds and its per-upload cap; on Hack the first three usage fields still describe that pool. ## Each person's records People add records; each signed-in person sees only their own, with status and history. The owner sees and updates all records. People request changes by appending linked change rows, preserving the original record and its history. Example uses: shop orders, RSVPs and event sign-ups, bookings and appointments, applications (jobs, clubs, hackathons), support requests, homework or assignment submissions, survey answers people can revisit, and a waitlist with “my place in line”. Use this pattern when someone asks for any of these. Choose resource and table names that fit the domain (`bookings`, `applications`, and so on), keeping the author-or-owner read rule above, a status column and a linked change table in the same database. Declare its foreign key so a person's change rows can reference only their own record. This pattern is for hosted Simple Host and small-box installs. ### Worked example: shop orders Create an `orders` SQLite resource with `storage_set_resource(site,"orders",body)` (or owner PUT): ```json {"kind":"sqlite","rules":{"version":1,"policies":[ {"command":"read","using":"visitor_id == auth.id || auth.role == \"owner\""}, {"command":"add","check":"auth.signed_in"}, {"command":"edit","using":"auth.role == \"owner\""}, {"command":"delete","using":"auth.role == \"owner\""} ]},"site_passcode":"inherit"} ``` Through owner `storage_sql_schema`, create these tables in two calls in that same database: ```sql CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT NOT NULL, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL, status TEXT DEFAULT 'placed', created_at TEXT) ``` ```sql CREATE TABLE order_changes ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('change','note','cancel_request')), details TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT ) ``` Both tables inherit the resource's rules: signed-in add, author-or-owner read, owner edit/delete. The server adds indexed `visitor_id TEXT`, stamps `created_at` on visitor inserts, and ignores client-sent identity and timestamps. A declared foreign key checks that the referenced order exists and belongs to the same customer, in the insert transaction (404 `invalid_reference` for a missing order and for another customer's order alike). Customers never rewrite or delete a placed order. They customise it by adding a change, a note, a cancellation request or a requested new quantity to `order_changes`; the original order and change history remain. The page shows “My orders”, each current status and its history, using two reads and matching `order_changes.order_id` to `orders.id` in the page. There is no `include=` option. ```html ``` ```js await SH.requireSignIn(); const db = SH.storage.sqlite('orders'); const orders = db.table('orders'); const changes = db.table('order_changes'); const receipt = await orders.add({item: 'Chai spice', quantity: 2}); await changes.add({order_id: receipt.last_insert_id, kind: 'change', details: 'Please change the quantity to 3'}); const mine = await orders.list({order: 'id', desc: 1, limit: 50}); const history = await changes.list({order: 'id', limit: 100}); // Both results contain only this customer's rows. Match history by order_id. // Follow each next_after cursor with the same order and direction. ``` The owner sees all orders and history through `storage_sql_query`. Each row's `visitor_id` in connector results is an opaque reference scoped to this site, not an account ID. Pass it directly in `storage_sql_query` or `storage_sql_execute` params for the same site. It lasts until the server restarts; read the row again if needed. Only when the owner asks "who placed order 12?" read `SELECT visitor_id FROM orders WHERE id = 12` and pass it to `storage_visitor_emails`, which gives the email they signed in with. Tell the person; never write the email into a page or into saved data. REST keeps its existing visitor IDs; use those with the owner-only `GET /v1/sites//storage/visitors?id=` route. The owner's view applies or acknowledges requests and updates the order's status or stage with `storage_sql_execute`, for example `UPDATE orders SET status=? WHERE id=?` with params `["packed",17]`. Keep the history when handling a request. Use the trusted owner dashboard/connector, or an admin page on the site (`get_page_recipe` topic `admin`): the owner signed in there with their account email lists every order (`orders.list({where:{status:'placed'}})`) and sets a status (`orders.edit(17, {status:'packed'})`). Never put an owner key in a page. The trade-off of an admin page: while the owner is signed in on their own site, a bug or a malicious script on its pages could act on that site's data, so write visitors' text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`. ### The owner adds a row for one person (SIM-358) On a table whose permissive read alternatives require the author or owner, the owner may add a row on behalf of one already-signed-in person instead of waiting for them to add it — a coach assigning a client's program, a tutor replying to a student's message. The row's `visitor_id` becomes that person's, exactly as if they had added it themselves, and a second server-owned column, `written_by`, reads `"owner"` (otherwise `""`, including a plain add with no `for`) so the person's own reads never mistake it for their own write: ```js // On the page, signed in as the owner on the site's own address. await SH.storage.sqlite('orders').table('orders').add( {item: 'House blend, 1 lb'}, {for: pickedVisitorId} ); ``` `storage_sql_execute` reaches the same path from a connector, by giving `table` and `values` instead of `sql` and `params`: ```json {"site": "", "name": "orders", "for": "client@example.com", "table": "orders", "values": {"item": "House blend, 1 lb"}} ``` `for` requires at least one author alternative and no permissive read alternative outside author-or-owner access; otherwise it is `for_requires_own`. `for` takes a `visitor_id` or the email that person signed in with (matched against their current sign-in email the same way `storage_visitor_emails`/`SH.me()` do, among people the server recorded as signed in on this site — never a raw username or OAuth-identity row alone, and never a guess among more than one match: `visitor_unknown` (404) if nobody matches, `visitor_email_ambiguous` if more than one does). There is no email binding before a first sign-in. It never fires `record.added` to the owner's own webhook subscriptions. `written_by` is added lazily, under the write lock, the first time a table is used this way — an existing author-tracked table works without resaving its rules — and is refused (`written_by_blocked`) rather than risk reshaping a table a trigger or view depends on; a trigger that got written_by onto the table some other way, and then rewrites it as a side effect of a `for` insert, is caught after the fact and the whole add is rolled back (`written_by_tampered`). The owner's raw SQL console (`storage_sql_execute` without `for`) refuses a statement naming `written_by`, in `execute` and `schema` alike, so a new trigger or view cannot name it either — but this is a name match, not a parser: a positional `INSERT INTO t VALUES (...)` naming no column is not caught, by design (no SQL parsing was added to try to catch it). As always, raw SQL can still set `visitor_id` directly too. Provenance through `written_by` holds for rows added through the table routes, `auth.js`, and `for`; the raw SQL console remains exactly as unrestricted on server columns as it already was. Changing a table's rules to grant wider reads exposes an owner-added row the same as any other row there; confirm the visibility change first. `for`, the pick list, and `storage_visitor_emails`'s `emails` direction are Host only (404 on Simple Hack and event storage): named viewers and this email resolution are not a Simple Hack concept. The owner's pick list of whom to add for: `SH.storage.people()` on the page, or `GET /v1/sites//storage/people` with the owner's key — people who have saved data here or are named viewers, each confirmed against the server's own sign-in record, never everyone who has merely signed in and never a raw table's content taken on trust. `storage_visitor_emails` also takes `emails` now, resolving each to the reference `for` takes, the same direction REST's `?email=` does. Worked example: `get_page_recipe` topic `people`. ## File buckets keep presets Create a `photos` file bucket. Choose preset `wall` for photos that visitors may view (authors can remove their own), or `records` for photos only the sender and the shop owner see: ```json {"kind":"files","preset":"wall","site_passcode":"inherit"} ``` ```js await SH.requireSignIn(); // preparedPhoto is a resized WebP Blob, below the single-upload cap. await SH.storage.files('photos').put(crypto.randomUUID() + '.webp', preparedPhoto); ``` A page may instead call relative REST routes with `credentials:'same-origin'` and `X-SH-CSRF: 1` for POST/PUT. The server takes identity from the site session. Preserve the form on a refusal; never widen access to make a save work. ## The same pattern for bookings Name the SQLite resource `bookings`, keeping the same policies. Through the owner schema route, create these tables in two calls: ```sql CREATE TABLE bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, appointment TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT DEFAULT 'requested', created_at TEXT) ``` ```sql CREATE TABLE booking_changes ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, booking_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES bookings(id), kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('change','note','cancel_request')), details TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT ) ``` The server adds indexed `visitor_id TEXT` to both tables as in the orders example. People add bookings and linked change rows; “My bookings” reads both tables and matches `booking_changes.booking_id` to `bookings.id`. Each person sees only their own status and history. The owner reads all bookings and changes, and updates status (for example, `confirmed`) through owner SQL. Visitor inserts use `INSERT OR ABORT` and RETURNING. Client primary-key and rowid values are refused. Foreign keys are enabled on every connection; hidden and missing parents both give `invalid_reference`. An existing resource with untrusted legacy SQL authorship needs deliberate owner migration before rules are saved; do not turn forged identities into per-person ownership. Visitor writes use `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_IP` (120,100ms) per site and client IP and `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_VISITOR` (60,200ms) per site and signed-in visitor. Reads, including POST `/query`, have no new rate limit; a 150-photo public gallery loads without consuming write tokens. Owner credentials are exempt. Reads never take the deploy mutex. Bodies are consumed before locking writes and quota checks. `SITE_STORAGE_WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` defaults to 2000; writes during deploy wait briefly, then return 503 `storage_busy` with Retry-After. Owner operations have `SITE_STORAGE_OWNER_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000); visitor writes have `SITE_STORAGE_VISITOR_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` (2000), and visitor SQLite queries have `SITE_STORAGE_VISITOR_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (1000). All SQLite executions, including owner queries and policy validation, share a per-site slot (one by default, `SITE_STORAGE_SITE_INFLIGHT`) and a process-wide semaphore: `SITE_STORAGE_SQL_CONCURRENCY=0` selects the CPU count. When full, `SITE_STORAGE_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS` (250) bounds waiting, then returns 503 with Retry-After. Writers always take the site lock before the SQLite slot. A visitor's fixed route permits at most 100 columns; the complete JSON query result is bounded by `SITE_STORAGE_SQL_RESULT_MAX_BYTES`. GET and HEAD are reads. KV allowance counts UTF-8 key bytes plus normalized JSON text bytes. `SITE_STORAGE_FILES_MAX_OBJECTS` defaults to 1000 committed objects per bucket, including empty/tiny files (507 `bucket_full`). File paths allow at most 16 segments. Own file lists use the existing `(site,resource,writer,path)` index and LIMIT before opening files; temporary `.upload-*` objects never appear. New keys and upload paths are normalized to NFC, including macOS decomposed names. Reads, deletes, listing prefixes and cursors accept exact legacy names. Own-list cursors follow scanned metadata so missing files cannot end paging early. SQLite uniqueness failures use a generic 409 `row_conflict`; schema names are not reflected to visitors. 507 `sqlite_full` describes engine allocation failures separately from the quota precheck's `site_full`. UNIQUE columns, KV keys and file paths are global within their table/resource. A failed create can reveal a collision; use opaque random identifiers or a visitor-specific namespace, never sensitive emails as unique keys. The server does not silently change owner-defined global uniqueness. `auth.js` retains raw query/execute for legacy compatibility; rules resources refuse visitor SQL and new visitor pages use `table().add/list`. `site_passcode:off` is an explicit owner choice: public resources stay accessible without unlocking. The shared clientIP helper still trusts the last X-Forwarded-For entry (N4). Deploy behind a local proxy that appends the real client address and prevents direct access to the app port; bare unproxied installs can spoof IP buckets.

---
name: website-deploy
description: Read this skill first, before calling any Simple Host connector tool, whenever someone wants a website or page made, put online or changed, including a plain "make me a website" that never names Simple Host (golden-host.invalid), even when the connector's own notes seem enough. It has the exact steps for business, agency, NGO, launch and client requests (booking, quote, contact, waitlist and sign-up forms, menus and prices updated from chat, client portals, reviews, photo uploads, owner-only pages) and covers own domains, short free addresses, passcodes, named viewers, versions, visitor numbers and the home page.
---

# Website Deploy

Simple Host publishes static websites at `https://sites.golden-host.invalid/<handle>/<site>/`, and each
site can save what visitors send (KV, SQLite and files), with visitor sign-in by emailed code or
Google. Use the signed-in Simple Host connector tools; if they are missing or signed out, ask the
person to connect Simple Host (https://golden-host.invalid/install.html). Never ask for, read or pass
on sign-in codes, API keys or passwords in chat. This server's `/auth.md` lists its configured sign-in methods.
Simple Host lists each operation individually for ChatGPT, OpenAI, and Codex. Call the named tool directly using its listed input schema. In other apps, use `find_tools` to look up an operation absent from your tool list, then call it with `run_tool` `{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}`.
On self-hosted installs, use the instance connector and returned URLs. Apps are operator opt-ins; use tool text when no screen is offered.
For ChatGPT, OpenAI, and Codex, offer to add the person's own photos once the page is live, and call `create_upload_link` when they say yes. In other apps, for photos the person has (a menu, listing, team, portfolio): call `create_upload_link` at once, even unasked. It shows a photo picker in the chat, or returns `photos_url` to give them. Never build an upload page for their own photos, and never ask them to convert, resize, or host photos elsewhere.

## 1. Decide what to build

People ask in a few words and never say who sees what. Pick the row, call `get_page_recipe` with
its topic, run the recipe's setup calls, and build the whole thing: the page, the storage with its
preset, sign-in only where the row says, and a line telling the owner how they see what comes in.

| They ask for | Topic | Who sees what |
|---|---|---|
| a photo picker, or their own photos on a page (menu dishes, a listing, team, portfolio) | none: `create_upload_link` | it shows a photo picker in the chat (or returns `photos_url`); then place the `images/` files. Do not build an upload page |
| a booking, appointment or table reservation (even a "booking request") | `booking` | the customer signs in with their email when they press Book, then sees their own bookings and status; the owner sees all and confirms from chat |
| a quote request, contact or enquiry form, waitlist, sign-up, volunteer or job application, feedback | `inbox` | anyone sends without signing in; only the owner reads, from chat |
| a menu, prices, opening hours, a stock list the owner changes | `public` | everyone reads; the owner changes it from chat with `storage_put_kv`, no republish |
| a client portal, client documents, a private page for one client | `portal` | one site per client, opened only to that client's email |
| a guestbook, comments, reviews or questions anyone may post without signing in | `comments` | everyone reads; anyone posts after a spam check (auth.js runs it); the owner removes posts, or approves each one first (`approve_first`). A server without the spam check (a self-hosted one with no Turnstile keys) refuses it with `spam_check_unavailable`: use `wall` |

## Which storage for which job (quick guide)
Each resource (and each SQLite table) has a **preset**: who may read, add, edit and delete. Each
action is `nobody` (the owner's tools only), `owner` (the owner's tools and the owner signed in on
the site), `own` (the signed-in person who added it, plus the owner), `signed-in` or `anyone`. The
server enforces it on every page request, whatever the page does.
| Preset | read / add / edit / delete | For |
| `public` | anyone / owner / owner / owner | a menu, prices, opening hours, a catalogue (the owner's own photos go through `create_upload_link` instead) |

| `inbox` | owner / anyone / owner / owner | quote requests, contact, waitlists, sign-ups, applications, feedback: sent without sign-in, only the owner reads (`"add":"signed-in"` only when the person asks for verified senders) |
| `wall` | anyone / signed-in / owner / own | guestbook, comments, reviews, a who's-coming list, visitors' photos (files) |

| `comments` | anyone / checked / owner / owner | a guestbook, comments, reviews or Q&A anyone posts without signing in; `checked` is anyone who passes a Cloudflare Turnstile spam check, which auth.js runs on its own when the page saves (kv and sqlite only; not on Simple Hack, nor on a server without Turnstile keys, which answers `spam_check_unavailable`: use `wall` there). `"approve_first": true` (sqlite) hides new posts until the owner sets `approved_at` |
| `records` | own / signed-in / owner / owner | each person's records: bookings, appointments, reservations, orders, RSVPs with a status |
| `personal` | own / signed-in / own / own | a wishlist, notes, settings, a profile, a cart across devices |
| `board` | signed-in / signed-in / signed-in / owner | a potluck or sign-up sheet, team tasks, a shared shopping list |
| `private` | owner / owner / owner / owner | the default: admin data, inventory, drafts |

## Access presets (Simple Host)
Every KV namespace, file bucket and SQLite table has an access matrix: four
actions, each given one "who" value.
- **read** lists and views; **add** creates a new key, row or path; **edit**
changes an existing one; **delete** removes one. For a KV or file `PUT` the
server decides add or edit by whether the key or path exists.
- **nobody**: only the owner's tools (key, connector). **owner**: the owner's
tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor
sign-in. **own**: the signed-in person who added the entry, plus the owner.
**signed-in**: anyone signed in on the site. **anyone**: anyone.
| Preset | read | add | edit | delete | For |
| `public` | anyone | owner | owner | owner | menus, catalogues, hours (the owner's own photos go through `create_upload_link` instead) |
| `inbox` | owner | anyone | owner | owner | contact, feedback, surveys, quote requests |
| `wall` | anyone | signed-in | owner | own | guestbooks, comments, reviews, public RSVP lists, visitors' photos |
| `comments` | anyone | checked | owner | owner | guestbooks, comments, reviews, questions posted without sign-in, after a spam check |
| `records` | own | signed-in | owner | owner | orders, bookings, applications, support tickets |
| `personal` | own | signed-in | own | own | wishlists, notes, saved settings, profiles |
| `board` | signed-in | signed-in | signed-in | owner | potluck and sign-up sheets, team task lists |
| `private` | owner | owner | owner | owner | the default: admin data, inventory, drafts |
Overrides change one action and are checked: `{"preset":"inbox","add":"signed-in"}`
(reported as `custom`, `based_on: inbox`); `{"preset":"custom","read":...,"add":...,"edit":...,"delete":...}`

default, and `tables` gives a table its own:
{"kind":"sqlite","preset":"private","tables":{"products":{"preset":"public"},"orders":{"preset":"records"}}}

**The owner on their own site.** The site's owner, signed in through visitor
sign-in with their account email on one of the site's own addresses (its site
host, a family address or its own domain; not the person host), acts with owner
rights for storage data only: every row, key and file, and edits and deletes
